excerpt: Code4SA Data Journalism School The three-month-long training programme will consist of a combination of theoretical and hands-on practical work. Participants will spend much of their time each day working in a data newsroom. In addition to data and social media journalism training, the school will also be a centre for news innovation. Through the newsroom, we will experiment with different approaches to delivering content to audiences, with an emphasis on actionable news. Code for South Africa is actively involved in ongoing projects that promote innovation in the media space through the use of data-driven storytelling and the school will play an important role in achieving this. Each intake will consist of up to eight junior to mid-level journalists. They will have the opportunity to gain practical data journalism skill-sets that will equip them to deliver compelling data-driven multimedia stories. The school will be run by a combination of experienced and award winning journalists, coders, data wranglers, analysts and content specialists. Modules will also include specialist topic lectures by high impact guest lecturers from local and international newsrooms. In order to promote data-driven storytelling in South Africa, the programme is heavily subsidised by our donors. The price for the programme is R18,000 over the three months. Media houses will be responsible for all costs of their trainees, including accommodation and transport. Course bursaries and monthly stipends available based on merit. This is a School of Data initiative kindly sponsored by Omidyar Network, Code for Africa, Knight Foundation and the Indigo Trust. Admission requirements Junior to mid-level journalists passionate about data Course dates February – April 2016 Application closing date 15 December 2015 Key outcomes - proficiency in working in the data pipeline - technical skill sets - ability to operate in a data newsroom - data-driven multi-media story portfolio For more information Strategic Objectives The strategic objectives of the Data Journalism School course are to: - Train a new generation of data journalists who have the skills to make sustainable changes within newsrooms; - Develop cuttingedge content, driven by internal research and executed by students, with technical support from an editorial and tech team; - Develop SETA accredited open source data journalism syllabus that is available for for incorporation into university degrees; - Develop a replicable model for a datadriven digital newsroom that produces multiplatform stories. Learning Outcomes Participants will achieve the following learning outcomes: - Proficiency in working in the data pipeline (i.e. the process of sourcing, cleaning, verifying, analysing and visualising data and storytelling across different platforms); - Gain technical skill sets (e.g. how to use various data scraping, cleaning, mapping and visualisation tools and spreadsheets); - The ability to operate in a datadriven newsroom - Build a multimedia story portfolio (Participants will be expected to regularly produce content. Project work will include quick turnaround newsdriven stories, as well as work on medium and longer term projects. Participants will be supported by an editorial team that will also include coders, data wranglers and analysts
